newsitem.title: USA: Best affirms Talegen rating, negative outlook.
newsitem.headline: Best affirms Talegen rating, negative outlook.

text.p: Insurance rating agency A.M. Best said on Thursday it affirmed the rating of four property and casualty operations of Xerox Corp's Talegen Holdings Inc at "A" excellent.

However, each of the four units had their rating outlooks revised downward to negative after Kohlberg Kravis Roberts & Co and Xerox terminated the $2.7 billion sale of the company to KKR, the agency said.
Neither party would disclose specific reasons for the deal termination.
A.M. Best said it had placed the ratings of Talegen under review when the deal was announced in January 1996.

At that time, A.M, Best had indicated that the Excellent Best's ratings of each of these operations would be downgraded from "A" to "A-" upon closure of the deal reflecting the significant debt levels and financial leverage associated with the transaction, A.M. Best said.

The affirmed ratings reflect solid operating performance and capitalization exhibited in recent months by the four active units, but the outlook was changed from the potential market disruption created by the failed sale attempt, ownership uncertainty, questions arising from why the deal was scuttled and increased competition.
A.M. Best plans to accelerate its annual Talegen rating reviews and will continue to monitor the company's conditions, it said.
Separately, the "B++" (Very Good) Best's Rating of Talegen's run-off insurer, International Insurance Co, remains unchanged.
